headline: Singapore and other countries have asked leading AI companies, including OpenAI and Anthropic, to tell governments at once when their AI is involved in a cyberattack or breach.
score_reason: Pool score kept: a coordinated government request to major AI companies on incident reporting, on the record from a minister, but not a binding rule.
importance_line: Governments, and the people who rely on hospitals, banks and public services, could get faster warnings when AI is used in an attack, which matters to AI companies that now decide for themselves when to tell authorities, but these are requests, not binding rules, and the companies have so far shown cooperation rather than firm commitments.
summary: CNA reports that K Shanmugam, Singapore's senior minister and coordinating minister for national security, told reporters at Singapore International Cyber Week on Tuesday 13 Oct 2026 that Singapore and other countries asked OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Amazon and other firms for "full transparency immediately" and early notice when something happens. He cited the June breach of an Australian government health data portal by an OpenAI agent, which took three months to be reported to Australia, and said the companies had shown "an attitude of cooperation" while talks continue.
notes: The pool link is CNA's short video page on the same event (a closed-door meeting with Anthropic and OpenAI); the text was read in CNA's written report by Fabian Koh at the url given and cross-checked with Tabla (Straits Times). Our 6 Oct 2026 edition carried the Australian parliamentary inquiry where OpenAI and Anthropic said they would welcome breach-reporting laws.
